```{julia}
# final epoch present in st (robust even if it's not exactly 10000)
final_epoch = maximum(st.epoch)

st_final = subset(st, :epoch => ByRow(==(final_epoch)))

best_per_task = combine(groupby(st_final, :task_id)) do sdf
    # pick row of max accuracy (if tie, first one)
    i = argmax(sdf.accuracies)
    (; best_bee_id = sdf.bee_id[i],
       best_accuracy = sdf.accuracies[i])
end

best_per_task = sort(best_per_task, :task_id)
best_per_task  # <- this is the mapping you asked for
```

```{julia}
# create a key table with pairs to remove
pairs_to_remove = select(best_per_task, :task_id, :best_bee_id => :bee_id)

# rows to remove:
act_remove = semijoin(act, pairs_to_remove, on=[:bee_id, :task_id])

# keep everything else:
act_keep = antijoin(act, pairs_to_remove, on=[:bee_id, :task_id])

# sanity checks
@show nrow(act) nrow(act_remove) nrow(act_keep)
```

```{julia}
using DataFrames

function suppressed_run_lengths(epochs::AbstractVector{<:Integer}, suppressed::AbstractVector{Bool})
    n = length(epochs)
    n == 0 && return Int[]
    # sort by epoch (important!)
    p = sortperm(epochs)
    e = epochs[p]
    s = suppressed[p]

    runs = Int[]
    cur = 0

    for i in 1:n
        gap_break = (i > 1) && (e[i] != e[i-1] + 1)   # treat missing epochs as breaking a run
        if gap_break
            if cur > 0
                push!(runs, cur)
                cur = 0
            end
        end

        if s[i]
            cur += 1
        else
            if cur > 0
                push!(runs, cur)
                cur = 0
            end
        end
    end

    if cur > 0
        push!(runs, cur)
    end

    return runs
end
```

```{julia}
start_epoch = 3000
act2 = subset(act_keep, :epoch => ByRow(>(start_epoch)))

run_df = combine(groupby(act2, [:bee_id, :task_id])) do sdf
    #runs = suppressed_run_lengths(sdf.epoch, sdf.suppressed)
    flipped = .!sdf.suppressed
    runs = suppressed_run_lengths(sdf.epoch, flipped)
    # return one row per run
    DataFrame(run_length = runs)
end

# This column contains all run lengths pooled across bees/tasks:
all_runs = run_df.run_length
```

```{julia}
dist_counts = combine(groupby(run_df, :run_length), nrow => :count)
sort!(dist_counts, :run_length)

total_runs = sum(dist_counts.count)
dist_counts.prob = dist_counts.count ./ total_runs

dist_counts
```

```{julia}
using Statistics

summary = (
    n_runs = length(all_runs),
    mean = mean(all_runs),
    median = median(all_runs),
    p90 = quantile(all_runs, 0.90),
    max = maximum(all_runs),
    std = std(all_runs),
)

summary
```
